title.narrative: Empowering Communities through Climate-Smart Agroforestry, Nutrition Enhancement, and School-Based Economic Tree Initiatives

description.narrative: ltpgtltbrgtThis project, led by the Foundation for Refugee Economic Empowerment (FREE), delivers a comprehensive suite of interventions to strengthen climate resilience, enhance food security, and improve nutritional outcomes for vulnerable communities in Jere, Borno State. Scheduled for January to August 2026. lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThe project is structured around three innovative pillars:lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThe Community-Centered "Resilience Hub (Farm School): Serving as a dynamic training center, the farm school will equip Community Resilience Champions and women-led households with advanced climate-smart techniques. These include smart agriculture practices such as mulching, trellising, seed selection, and irrigation. The hub will also demonstrate innovative aquaculture methods as Azolla farming a low-cost, readily available, high-protein feed for poultry, fish, and other animals. Additionally, it will feature Advanced Black Soldier Fly (BSF) larvae feed production, by establishing a BSF insectarium for waste-to-protein conversion. This system produces BSF larvae as a high-protein substitute feed for fish and poultry, with a protein concentration of up to 90%+ using purely food was.ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtltbrgtDiversified Livelihoods for Resilience Champions: Target farmers are organized into two specialized streams. Agro-Aqua Pastorals focuses on integrated livestock and aquaculture (poultry, goats, Azolla, BSF), while Climate-Smart Crop Producers specializes in bio-fortified crops supported by fertilizers and UV solar food dryers for preservation and value addition.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtCross-Cutting Nutrition Resilience Initiatives:ltbrgtThese include a child-centered agroforestry model where school children plant and nurture fruit-bearing and erosion-control trees ( Moringa, mango, cashew, Leucaena etc) centered around one designated school garden fitted with tools and form social agro school clubs Cash-for-Work schemes to build and maintain community assets such as drainage systems, solar pumps, BSF insectarium, Azolla ponds, school gardens, and the Resilience Hubthe targeted provision of SAFE stoves, tools, and training to women-led households with children under five, coupled with unconditional support. Disability and gender inclusion are mainstreamed throughout all activities.lt/pgtltpgtCapacity building is conducted on all project components to ensure the active engagement and sensitization of beneficiaries, which includes:ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtlt/pgtltpgtltbrgt1)School Club Facilitation Session in child-centered school garden set-uplt/pgtltpgt2)Farmer Field School (FFS) training in resilience hublt/pgtltpgt3)Nutrition Food Preservationlt/pgtltpgt4)PSEAH Protection Mainstreamingltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtltbrgtDirectly benefiting 1,200 individuals and indirectly reaching 5,000 community members, this holistic approach reduces dependency on aid and builds intergenerational resilience. By integrating proven methods with innovative practices, the project fosters self-sufficiency and equips communities to withstand climate shocks, directly contributing to SDG 2 (Zero Hunger) and SDG 13 (Climate Action)ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThe initiative is built on FREE's proven track record, which includes a 98% survival rate for economic trees in school compounds and the successful distribution of agricultural inputs to over 22,000 farming households in the region.ltbrgtlt/pgt
